decision.title: Long streams: the text method streams, long text runs grow linearly, streamed elements grant steps (packet stream-1)
decision.summary: Long text runs in the arena tree grow linearly, the takes the text method, and each element a streamed parse reads gives the evaluation a of 500 steps.

item.p: Quadratic memory, the cause: a streamed principal source whose stylesheet wrote text with method="text" (an xsl:value-of per record) went to the principal stream (), which serialized as it went only for the xml method; for text the events built the result tree. The arena tree's text store moves a pending text run that outgrows its block to a new one; past the largest block (1 MiB) the new block had exactly the room the run needed, so every text event copied the whole run into a fresh block and left the old one in the arena: quadratic time and memory (5,000 records of 1 KB, 4.7 MB of text, were killed at 13.5 GB). Any tree with one long text node made of many events had it (html, xml with indent, constructed trees).

Fixes: (1) src/arena_tree.c: a run that outgrows the largest block gets room for as much again as it holds: O(n) bytes copied, at most about 4n of blocks. (2) The streamed serialization (src/serialize_xml.c, glossary ) takes the text method without normalization-form (sxml_serialization_streams): a tree builder of its own writes each text event's characters as it comes and nothing for the other events (Serialization 4.0, 8: the string values of the text nodes in document order; disabled escaping changes nothing there, XSLT 4.0, 26.1.8). normalization-form is left to the built tree: the serializer normalizes a text node at a time, and two events' characters could combine. (3) The xml method's streamed serialization joins adjacent text into one node before writing it (); it now writes the joined text in parts of 64 KiB when that writes the same characters (not in a CDATA section, not normalizing), so one long text node is not held whole either.

Other methods: html and xml with indent, canonical, doctype or standalone still build the tree (now linear: 18.8 MB of html text, 75.6 MB); json and adaptive (no tree by default, 26.1) deliver the raw sequence of text nodes (linear, 166 MB for 18.8 MB; SERE0023 for json and many items, as the specification says). A streamed html writer is not made here.

The step limit for long streams: 's 10^8 steps stopped the streamed identity of a 93 MB document (2.7 million elements) after 68 MB, from the CLI as from the package. Decided: each element a streamed document's parse reads grants the evaluation 500 steps (SXML_EVALUATOR_STREAMED_ELEMENT_STEP_COUNT, sxml_dynamic_context_grant_steps, internal: the steps taken are lowered, never below none, after each resume of the parse; glossary ). The identity takes about 50 an element (its attributes and text included), so a stream that does up to ten times that per element runs within the bound; a loop that reads no more input stops at the bound plus the grant of what was read, at most 500 steps an element; evaluations of trees, and the bound itself, are unchanged ('s "a runaway query stops in about 8 s" holds for them). Rejected: a larger default (it weakens the bound for every query), and a grant per event taken by a STREAM task (a body that reads full windows or skips content would take steps for elements it never takes as events).

JavaScript: createProcessor({ maximumEvaluationStepCount }), sxml_processor_limits.maximum_evaluation_step_count (0 and absent: sxml's default; a whole number below 2^53, else RangeError). The export sxml_javascript_processor_create takes a request struct (failing allocation, feature mask, code languages, step count; wasm32 offsets 0, 4, 8, 16, asserted) instead of three arguments, and sxml_host_processor_configuration gains maximum_evaluation_step_count at its end (the host shim, not a public header: does not apply; Kotlin's JNI uses designated initializers, Swift's memberwise call passes 0, not compiled here). The CLI has no step flag and gets none: no command needed one, and the grant makes its streams run. README and the book's JavaScript and performance chapters say so.

Measured (release CLI, peak resident set; Node.js 22 with the wasm module, a chunk source and a writeSync sink): method text, 20,000 records of 1 KB: 11.0 MB 0.55 s (before: out of memory), byte-identical to method xml (11.0 MB 0.5 s); Node 10.3 MB of module memory, 1.3 s (: 4 GB). The streamed identity of 93 MB: before stopped at the bound after 15.9 s, after the whole output in 23.2 s, 11.0 MB; Node 52.6 s, 10.7 MB of module memory, 160 MB resident. Method text over the 93 MB file: 11.0 MB, 13.6 s; Node 29.8 s.

Tests: arena_tree long_text_runs_grow_linearly (a 2 MB node from 2,000 events allocates 5.2 MB); evaluator_stream principal cases for the text method and one long text node under xml (peaks 208 KB and 400 KB under a 1 MB limit) and streamed_elements_grant_steps (under 10^6 steps the streamed identity of 90,000 elements runs; the unstreamed one and a loop after two records stop); javascript/streams 2 new cases. Debug (ASan, UBSan), release and wasm: 407 of 407. XT40, 96 sets (si-, sf-, sx-*, streamable, accumulator, merge, iterate, source-document, streaming-fallback, stream-available, output, result-document, value-of; 3,465 cases, release driver, case by case): 3,382 passed before and after, no outcome differs. sxml.wasm 13,452,276 bytes stripped, 2,423,328 gzipped (budget 14,000,000 / 2,800,000, not raised).
